# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Age:** sixteen years old  <sub>[v1 c33 P46](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0046)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c14 P68](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0068), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is described as plain. She exhibits a lady-like demeanour.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## Personality

Jane is steady, sensible, composed, and practical, with nerves that are rarely rattled. She is plodding and conscientious in her work, though unpoetical in her views. She believes in maintaining strict order in the classroom and is willing to punish pupils who disobey or make funny speeches. Despite her outward composure, she can succumb to tears during emotional moments.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008), [v2 c11 P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065)_

## History

Jane attended school in Avonlea, where she prepared a dialogue with Ruby Gillis and Diana Barry under Miss Stacy, and studied for the Entrance examination to Queen's Academy. Despite insisting she would not shed a tear when their teacher Mr. Phillips left, she wept so hard she had to borrow her brother's handkerchief. She passed her exams and attended Queen's Academy, taking the Second Class course and taking top honors in domestic science. After graduating, she accepted a teaching post in Newbridge, earning a place on the School Inspector's Roll of Honor. Outside of teaching, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, chaired a committee to raise funds to paint the hall, and helped canvass local residents.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003)_
